coding_boundary: Candidate texture-language episodes were coded from the already-pinned Artemis II transcript corpus. No new LOLA, WAC, Diviner, topography, albedo, geologic-unit, or control-target values were accessed for Stage 7B.
shared_endpoint: LOLA median absolute slope over prospectively fixed equal-physical-area regions

candidates.exclusion: The pair is the already-scored Stage 7A outcome and compares a 98.22 km crater with a 536.37 km basin. It cannot become a new held-out or morphology-matched observation by reuse.

anchors: Hertzsprung is that nice packed and smoother
around Hertzsprung looks like to me
candidates.exclusion: Orientale supplied the exploratory observation that formed this lane and was prospectively excluded from Stage 7A evaluation. Reintroducing it would convert calibration material into a held-out claim.

Two observers support the absolute description, but the transcript supplies no new non-Orientale matched comparator. Selecting an outcome-favorable comparator later would not be a controlled directional test.

anchors: just to the north of Vavilov
where the craters start again it starts to smooth back out
candidates.direction: Pumice-like patch rougher than adjacent smoother patch
candidates.exclusion: The words provide no recoverable boundaries, offsets, sizes, or unique named features. A disk chosen after map inspection would manufacture the localization.

anchors: difference in the texture of the ground
more jagged and pumice-y of Vavilov in west
west which is much more consolidated and firm and packed
candidates.direction: Central loose region differs from packed western region
candidates.exclusion: The observation deliberately describes regional continua rather than two bounded targets. Ohm and Vavilov names are landmarks, not sufficient polygons.

anchors: Glushko's got some primary rays, but they're jagged, right?
candidates.exclusion: This is an interrogative cue without a transcript-confirmed response, comparison target, ray-sector geometry, or recoverable boundary.

anchors: I can't see any swirls there
The albedo of Reiner Gamma is about a 7
candidates.endpoint: photometrically normalized reflectance and within-region dispersion
candidates.direction: Reiner Gamma is relatively uniform with a darker center
candidates.exclusion: This is a plausible separate albedo test, not a second observation on the shared LOLA roughness endpoint. Mixing it into the roughness panel would make a successful bundle uninterpretable.

anchors: comparing the brightness of Ohm rays to Glushko rays
candidates.endpoint: photometrically normalized reflectance contrast of frozen ray annuli
candidates.direction: Glushko and Ohm rays are similar, with Glushko slightly brighter
candidates.exclusion: This is the strongest cross-axis candidate, but ray sectors and local-background controls are not specified by the transcript and its endpoint is reflectance, not LOLA slope. It requires a separately frozen albedo experiment.

candidates.endpoint: mapped relative geologic age and degradation class
candidates.exclusion: The current research pass exposed official age context after Stage 7A. This may be reported as source concordance later, but it is no longer a held-out prediction and cannot repair the roughness panel.
